name: Skippi Ice Pops
tagline: Hyderabad ice-pop brand that ships at room temperature for home freezing
excerpt: Skippi Ice Pops landed the first all-shark deal on Shark Tank India, in Season 1, Episode 6.
content:
Skippi sells ice pops that travel and sit on shelves at room temperature; buyers freeze them at home. Husband and wife Ravi and Anuja Kabra started the Hyderabad brand in 2021 and pitched it in the sixth episode of Shark Tank India, aired on 27 December 2021.

All five sharks on the panel that day joined one offer, ₹1 crore for 15%, which made Skippi the show's first all-shark deal. Later reports say Peyush Bansal came in after filming, taking the total to ₹1.2 crore for 18%.

Since then Skippi has raised a ₹10 crore pre-Series A in 2024 and a ₹12 crore extension in 2025. Inc42's filing data shows revenue fell sharply in FY25 from the year before, and the company is loss-making, so the post-show story is mixed.

deal.terms: All-shark deal on air; later reports say Peyush Bansal joined after the show, taking it to ₹1.2 crore for 18%

shark_tank.pitch_summary: The Kabras pitched ice pops that need no cold chain until the buyer freezes them. Every shark in the room joined a single offer.

faq.q: Did Skippi get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. All five sharks on the panel jointly offered ₹1 crore for 15%, the show's first all-shark deal.
Yes. It raised fresh funding in June 2025 and sells online and through retail outlets.
Inc42's filing data shows total revenue of about ₹8.3 crore in FY25, down from about ₹20.2 crore in FY24.

lessons: Our analysis: removing the cold chain was the real innovation; it opened small shops that cannot run freezers.
Our analysis: fast growth after TV exposure can reverse, so later filings matter more than the on-air excitement.
notes: Original ask (₹45 lakh for 5%) appears only on Wikipedia/blogs, so it is left out. Deal terms conflict: on air ₹1 Cr for 15% from five sharks (BS/ANI 2021); later ₹1.2 Cr for 18% with Peyush (BS 2025, Inc42 2024 'all six sharks'). Better India 2023 also gives ₹1 Cr for 15%. The ₹100 Cr valuation in BS 2025 is a target, not a valuation, so it is left out.
